title: Why Electrification Is Gaining Traction in Manufacturing

## Why Electrification Is Gaining Traction in Manufacturing


Technological advancements and evolving market pressures are changing the global manufacturing landscape, prompting many companies to look at their processes and operations for opportunities to improve efficiency.


Electrification is one way manufacturers can keep up with these advancements; however, the main need for electrification is changing. Initially driven by sustainability initiatives, many manufacturers today are adopting electric technologies to reduce energy consumption, lower operating costs and improve productivity.


#### Insight into electrification


Electrification replaces pneumatic and other non-electric products and processes with electric alternatives. These electric options often include modern technology, such as controls, connectivity and real-time process monitoring.


Real-time visibility allows manufacturers to make more informed business decisions by providing accurate insights into material usage, system performance and production efficiency.


#### Reducing energy consumption and emissions


Transitioning manufacturing processes to electric alternatives can help manufacturers maintain productivity and efficiency while reducing emissions and energy consumption.


By implementing electric solutions into manufacturing processes, companies can better position their operations to meet emission regulations while increasing production output without significantly increasing energy usage.


#### Driving consistency and throughput through automation


Electrification not only helps manufacturers reduce their carbon footprint and manage energy costs; it also creates opportunities to increase throughput and improve operational performance.


When combined with trending technological advancements like automation, electrification can influence productivity. Automation helps ensure processes are executed as planned, regardless of operator experience, while reducing manual tasks and labor requirements. By implementing process control and monitoring, manufacturers can improve efficiency without compromising quality or production results.
